settings.name: Cloudflare Pages and Workers
settings.who: Someone deploying a static site, an Astro or Next.js build, or a small full-stack app, who also wants DNS and a CDN in one account.
settings.problem: Getting a built site onto the internet, fast, with previews per branch and no server to maintain. It is what the GitHub Actions and Cloudflare deployment guide targets.
settings.limits: The Workers runtime is not Node.js; libraries that expect a filesystem or long-running processes need adapting. The free tier's Workers limits are 100k requests a day and 10 ms CPU per request — generous for a marketing site, not for a busy application. Pages allows 500 deploys a month on the free plan.
settings.alternative: If your site is a handful of HTML files and you already have hosting that serves them over HTTPS with a certificate that renews, you do not need to move.
settings.basis: Described from Cloudflare's own pricing and Pages documentation, read 24 September 2026. Not independently benchmarked by us.

settings.name: Netlify
settings.who: Someone who wants Git-push deploys and preview URLs with the least configuration, and does not need Cloudflare's edge runtime.
settings.problem: Connecting a repository to a live site and getting a preview URL per pull request without writing a pipeline.
settings.limits: Bandwidth and build-minute allowances are not stated on the pricing page; check the current limits before assuming the free tier fits. The first paid tier is $9 a month per member, so a two-person team is $18.
settings.alternative: If you are already deploying through GitHub Actions to somewhere that works, this is a lateral move.
settings.basis: Described from Netlify's own pricing page, read 24 September 2026. Not used by this site.

settings.name: UptimeRobot
settings.who: Anyone responsible for a live site who would currently find out it was down from a customer.
settings.problem: The cheapest useful maintenance check there is: something watching the site from outside and telling you before anyone else notices. The maintenance checklist opens with this check for a reason.
settings.limits: The free plan checks every five minutes, so a short outage can fall between checks. It tells you the page responded — not that a form still delivers or a certificate is about to expire. Those stay manual.
settings.alternative: If your host already alerts you on downtime and you have tested that it does, you have this covered.
settings.basis: Free plan (50 monitors, 5-minute interval) and the $13/month Solo tier read from UptimeRobot's pricing page on 24 September 2026. Not used by this site.

settings.name: Plausible Analytics
settings.who: A site owner who wants to know what pages are read without running Google Analytics, and without adding a cookie banner.
settings.problem: Page-level traffic you can act on, from a script that sets no cookies and collects no personal data. Search Console tells you what Google served; this tells you what happened on the site.
settings.limits: It is deliberately shallow: no user-level journeys, no cohorts, no session replay. If you need to follow one person across visits, this is the wrong tool by design. From $9/month at 10k monthly pageviews, with a 30-day trial and no card.
settings.alternative: On a small store, Shopify's own analytics plus Search Console already answer most questions. Add this when you want page-level data the platform does not give you.
settings.basis: Used by this site. Installed on sitebuilderstack.com on 17 September 2026 and running on every page since. Pricing and trial terms read from plausible.io on 24 September 2026.

settings.name: Buttondown
settings.who: Someone whose site has readers but no shop, who wants a list without a marketing suite.
settings.problem: Writing to people who asked to hear from you, in plain text, without automations you will never build.
settings.limits: Deliberately minimal: no visual builder, no CRM, no complex segmentation. Base paid pricing is not stated on the pricing page — check before committing. The first 100 subscribers are free.
settings.alternative: If you sell through Shopify, its own customer list and email tool already exist and already hold your buyers — that is what this site uses. Adding a second list is a decision, not a default.
settings.basis: Described from Buttondown's pricing page, read 24 September 2026. Not used by this site.
